q1: False. HTML is a markup language, not a programming language. It describes structure and meaning but has no logic, loops, or conditionals.
q2: C - Structuring content and giving it semantic meaning. HTML's job is structure and semantics; CSS handles styling (A), JavaScript handles interactivity (B), and HTML doesn't compile to machine code (D).
q3: WHATWG (Web Hypertext Application Technology Working Group). The WHATWG maintains the HTML Living Standard as a continuously evolving specification.
q4: Browser sends request → Server responds with HTML → Browser parses HTML and builds DOM → Browser paints page. This is the correct order of the request-render cycle.
